executiveSummary: GM0376 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Identity, 2025 municipality totals, the generalized boundary, nine CBS neighbourhoods, BAG/BRT settlement context, six NWB links, null handling, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, exact zero-intensity behavior and event-attributable essential-service person-hours are coherent. Release nevertheless remains correction-required for three reproducible spatial-evidence defects. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset assigns persistent municipality-wide inundation stress without selecting an Eemmeer, Gooiergracht, regional-defence or major-river hydraulic pathway. Its neighbourhood order is exactly identical to the pluvial order even though current local evidence places rainwater nuisance between Bijvanck and Blaricummermeent and describes the Gooiergracht as a managed system with heavy-rain, drought, wastewater, pump, weir and Eemmeer dependencies. A focused synthetic wildfire placed at the official centre of BU03760103 Blaricummer Heide ranks that containing neighbourhood fifth, below De Kampen roughly 5.009 km away. The coastal preset correctly gives Blaricum zero direct seawater stress but still creates wind-driven service impacts; these components need clearer headline separation. The public layer contains 22 water assets, five education locations and two administration points, while provider lookup identifies Liander, PWN and Ziggo, but none supplies operational topology, live state, backup, stocks, crews or restoration commitments. All eight cross-municipality service views honestly remain NWB-derived logical transfer proxies. Outputs are deterministic planning estimates, not forecasts, observed outages, evacuation capacity or an asset-level digital twin.

Blaricummer Heide, Blaricummermeent, Bijvanck, De Kampen, Eemmeer-Blaricum and Stichtsebrug are distinct official neighbourhood geometries, not interchangeable hazard footprints or service areas.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024 — definitief
supports: Blaricum is part of the region; much of the region lies below NAP, surface water and water-management assets are important, and forests, heath, water and reed areas are material regional context.

Overstroming, storm/wind/neerslag, cold, heat, electricity loss, speech/data loss, cyberattack and nature fire are all retained risks; nature fire became a priority risk because climate change raises probability and impact.
Vital roads, rail, waterways, pipelines and high-voltage connections have cross-boundary dependencies, and smoke, flood, fire and extreme-weather effects do not stop at administrative borders.

The RRP is strategic expert judgement adopted on a four-year cycle and scoped to regional, above-local crises; it is not a live feed, GM0376 hazard footprint, service topology, probability raster or restoration forecast. No explicit machine API or redistribution licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Besluitenlijst college 3 december 2024 — Aanpak wateroverlast Laagwaterslootpark
supports: Inspection and resident complaints identify water nuisance at Park Laagwatersloot between Bijvanck and Blaricummermeent.
The Laagwatersloot is part of the area's water management and nuisance reduces park usability and harms planting and trees.

This is a dated local decision and observed/problem context, not a machine-readable design storm, depth grid, flood probability, sewer model or live incident feed; no fixed update cadence or explicit data licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Watergebiedsplan Gooiergracht and adopted 2026 draft measures
evidenceSources.edition: project page updated February 2026; draft adopted 2026-03-31
supports: The 152-hectare Gooiergracht area includes Blaricum, Laren and Eemnes and has long-standing heavy-rain water nuisance, dry-period shortage, vulnerable banks and incomplete system knowledge.

The channel is fed for about 95% by treated wastewater from the Hilversum and Blaricum treatment plants; water level, water quality, supply, drainage, soil, subsidence, weirs, pump function and municipal sewers are coupled concerns.
The 2026 draft measures include fixed target levels, controllable replacement weirs, widening the channel and a culvert, explicitly in combination with municipal sewer changes.

A related official AGV page states the roughly five-kilometre channel drains Gooi water through five weirs to a pump discharging to Eemmeer. These are current planning/mechanism facts, not live control state, hydraulic connectivity or a 72-hour forecast; no public machine layer, fixed data cadence or explicit reuse licence accompanies the project page.

evidenceSources.title: Droogtemaatregelen 2026 — extra pumps at the Blaricum lock
evidenceSources.edition: live situation page updated 2026-09-01; Blaricum action dated 2026-05-12
supports: AGV deployed extra pumps at the Blaricum lock on 12 May 2026 because drought lowered the Blaricummermeent water level.
The page was updated on 1 September 2026 and distinguishes current regional phase, restrictions, water levels and temporary measures.

This is authoritative observed/current operations context with event-driven updates, not a stable calibration, promised API, permanent asset capability or future scenario; explicit redistribution terms are not stated.

Named objects include RWZI Blaricum, Poldergemaal Eemmeer, Opvoergemaal Blaricummermeent, Poldergemaal Gooise Zomerkade, Blaricummermeent sluice and Blaricummermeentstuw.

Kunstwerken IMWA and companion Waterketen DAMO at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are machine-readable OGC Features under CC BY-SA 4.0. Contributor completeness varies and the landing pages do not promise one contractual refresh cadence; retain object and retrieval timestamps.

The layer is partial official context and currently affectsSimulation=false. Object presence/status does not prove capacity, hydraulic connectivity, control logic, current operation, emergency power or restoration time.

evidenceSources.title: Natuurbrandrisico — current regional phase and mechanism guidance

supports: The current Gooi en Vechtstreek indicator is phase 1; Brandweer states the phase is adjusted around midnight when needed and derives it from measurements, weather and field observations.
Forest, heath and grass fires can develop quickly in dry periods; evacuation direction, road access, precise location and mobile reach are operationally relevant.

The current phase is contextual only and must not be applied retrospectively to canonical T+0–72 exercises. No documented public bulk API, fixed archival contract or explicit redistribution licence is provided.

transport.summary: Six NWB-derived routes and scheduled transit stops are structurally valid but do not establish live capacity, evacuation or physical utility transfer.
notes: The graph has A27 links to Almere and Eemnes; A1 links to Huizen and Laren; and N527/N526 links to Huizen, totaling nominal scenario capacity 1,340.
No ProRail station lies inside the generalized boundary; 13 grouped GTFS stop-area records include Blaricum P+R, Crailo P+R, Dorp, De Maten, Viersloot and other local stops.
NWB is static road geometry and GTFS is scheduled transit. Neither supplies live closure, congestion, bridge state, vehicle operation, responder access, evacuation destination or throughput.
The same routes are reused for all eight services only as logical transfer proxies.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative sources establish local water, heath/fire, age, power and cross-boundary dependencies, but operational topology and capacity remain unavailable.
notes: The application intersects 22 HWH water assets, five current DUO education-location records and two KVK public-administration points with GM0376; no RIVM 2026 acute-care questionnaire location lies inside the generalized boundary.

The absence of an RIVM acute-care point is not an absence of healthcare demand or external hospital dependency, and an education/administration registration is not a shelter, staffing or incident-capacity record.

A current provider-territory query at the municipal reference point resolves Liander for electricity/gas, PWN for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed-media context; no drainage polygon is returned. Provider areas are responsibility context, not topology or state.
E05–E07 reveal wastewater-to-Gooiergracht, level-control, pump, sewer and Eemmeer dependencies that the causal graph does not encode.

No sensitive/operational cable, pipe, sewer, telecom, care, warehouse or response topology; live availability; backup endurance; priority-customer list; stock; crew or restoration commitment was inferred.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact zero-intensity semantics, determinism, monotonic cumulative burden, route bounds and local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0376 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 28.44 seconds on the initial focused run.
Every canonical preset at intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; state is finite/bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; and route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciles municipality population 12,947, affected population 5,923 and all eight demand/delivery balances, with maximum floating-point discrepancy 3.56e-15.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: River/pluvial neighbourhood maps and an explicit Blaricummer-Heide wildfire source do not follow Blaricum's hydraulic or source geometry.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-463 reduces named major-river exposure to municipality-centre distance from three coarse line segments and creates persistent scalar stress without a selected defence, connected footprint, depth/arrival/recession scenario or Eemmeer/Gooiergracht pathway.

At T+24 and T+72 the river preset retains normalized inundation stress 0.457414 and severity 0.142211, with 2,012 then 2,040 modeled people under pressure and 35,120 then 145,993 cumulative proxy person-hours.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3405 and 3416-3418 multiply municipality severity by one deterministic neighbourhood hash. River and pluvial therefore have the identical exact nine-neighbourhood hazard order: De Kampen, Blaricummermeent, Stichtsebrug, Blaricum-Dorp, Blaricummer Heide, Eemmeer-Blaricum, Bijvanck, Crailo, Warandepark-De Eng.
The pluvial order is unsupported by E04's observed Laagwaterslootpark context between Bijvanck and Blaricummermeent and E05–E07's actual catchment, sewer, level, pump, weir and Eemmeer mechanisms.

In a focused synthetic T+24 wildfire with source [5.21718211689071, 52.27399091655463] at the official centre of BU03760103 Blaricummer Heide, that source neighbourhood ranks only 5/9 at 0.506656. BU03760106 De Kampen ranks first at 0.596843 despite its centre being about 5.009 km from the source; source-distance to Blaricummer Heide is zero.

The unsupported-hazard UI safety treatment at apps/web/src/components/MapView.tsx:474-488 and Inspector.tsx:67-76 is not activated because GM0376 currently emits derived-screening/synthetic rather than unsupported spatial evidence.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight balances and causal stages are inspectable, but magnitudes are not calibrated to Blaricum's providers, water system, facilities, mobility or supply chain.
notes: Compound T+24 availability was power 0.139676, water 0.667954, drainage 0.494095, gas 0.821519, telecom 0.601169, mobility 0.265828, facilities 0.764579 and supply 0.711922.

E03 supports cross-boundary electricity/ICT/vital-infrastructure cascades; E04–E07 support the direction of local water/drainage dependencies, but no source calibrates those exact availability, demand, delivery or repair values.

The causal graph has no named RWZI Blaricum, Gooiergracht, Poldergemaal Eemmeer, Opvoergemaal Blaricummermeent, sluice, PWN source/treatment node, Liander station/feeder, radio site, school/care/shelter role or emergency-stock depot.

Official zero-resident neighbourhoods receive non-zero activity demand where non-residential/business context is available, which is preferable to population-only allocation, but the coefficients are transparent planning assumptions rather than measured occupancy or criticality.
All eight service views reuse the same six NWB-derived routes and total nominal 1,340; emitted transferSemantics is logical-proxy.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve scenario confidence, operations assumptions, dependency ordering and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, drivers, local vulnerability/demand factors, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Operational controls and time-gated interventions are labeled scenario assumptions; shared road-derived utility flows remain logical proxies.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure against a matched no-event baseline and are not observed outage-hours, casualties, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water repair gating behaves consistently, but local recession, asset, backup and crew evidence does not calibrate first-72-hour restoration.
notes: For river flooding, normalized inundation stress remains 0.457414 through T+72 and recoveryProgress remains exactly zero for all eight services; drainage availability is 0.670375 at T+24/T+72 and facilities changes slightly from 0.736454 to 0.725299 through dependency dynamics.

For compound, inundation stress remains 0.532322 at T+72 and recoveryProgress is zero for all eight services; power remains limiting at 0.139676 and cumulative proxy burden reaches 476,787 person-hours.

This verifies the sustained-flood repair guard and avoids claiming repairs through active water. It does not validate the underlying persistent water fields, which are unselected generic screens rather than local hydraulic recession estimates.

Coastal direct water/headline severity remains zero, while scenario wind produces T+24 pressure 0.241856, 1,858 modeled people under pressure and 10,536 event-attributable person-hours; pressure falls to 0.121271 and affected population to zero by T+72.

No source supplies event-specific asset damage, control-state history, spare power, staffing, dispatch, mutual aid, stock, access or restoration commitment; all response multipliers remain bounded scenario assumptions.

findings.summary: A coarse major-river proximity field presents unsupported persistent Blaricum inundation without a selected local hydraulic pathway.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-463 computes exposure only from municipality-centre distance to three approximate Rhine/Meuse/IJssel line segments. At both T+24 and T+72 the canonical preset reports normalized inundation-stress amplitude 0.457414, severity 0.142211 and zero recovery across every service; modeled people under pressure are 2,012/T+24 and 2,040/T+72, with event-attributable person-hours rising from 35,120 to 145,993. E03 recognises flood risk regionally, while E04–E07 identify Blaricum's concrete Laagwatersloot, Gooiergracht, wastewater, pump, weir, sluice and Eemmeer mechanisms. None selects a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel breach, defence, connected footprint, water level, return period, arrival or recession supporting the displayed local amplitude. This is municipality-specific evidence of a shared proximity-screen defect, not a claim that Blaricum is flood-safe.
findings.action: Mark GM0376's direct major-river result unsupported/Unknown and suppress its local rank and direct downstream consequence until an expert selects a named/versioned hydraulic scenario. Preserve separate Eemmeer, regional-water, pluvial and indirect network context. Durable integration should sample an approved LIWO/AGV depth-arrival-duration footprint and retain source mechanism, failed defence, scenario ID, probability class, units, version, no-data, licence and uncertainty.

findings.summary: The neighbourhood cloudburst ranking ignores Blaricum's observed nuisance location and managed drainage geography.
findings.evidence: E04 locates water nuisance at Park Laagwatersloot between Bijvanck and Blaricummermeent. E05–E07 identify the Gooiergracht/RWZI/sewer/level/pump/weir/Eemmeer chain and 22 intersecting official assets. Nevertheless packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3405 and 3416-3418 use one region hash, yielding the identical exact order for river and pluvial at T+24: De Kampen, Blaricummermeent, Stichtsebrug, Blaricum-Dorp, Blaricummer Heide, Eemmeer-Blaricum, Bijvanck, Crailo, Warandepark-De Eng. Pluvial severity is 0.430517 in five-resident De Kampen and only 0.358358 in dense Bijvanck. No rain raster, surface depression, slope, sewer catchment, receiving-water level, asset connectivity or control state governs the order.
findings.action: Until a licensed stress-test/hydraulic surface is sampled, mark neighbourhood pluvial distribution unsupported and prohibit rank-based dispatch or evacuation use. Prefer a municipality/AGV native stress-test export; otherwise use the CC BY 4.0 Klimaateffectatlas raster only as national indicative context. Retain storm definition, cell size, units, edition, no-data, uncertainty and licence. Use AHN, IMWA/DAMO/GWSW and land cover only as disclosed covariates, never infer operation from object presence.

findings.summary: An explicit Blaricummer-Heide ignition does not control the neighbourhood map presented as local wildfire impact.
findings.evidence: E02 establishes the official BU03760103 Blaricummer Heide geometry; E03 makes nature fire a regional priority and identifies forest/heath context; E08 describes drought/weather and access-sensitive wildfire behavior. A focused synthetic T+24 run placed the source at its official centre [5.21718211689071, 52.27399091655463]. Municipality direct-fire intensity is 0.523602, smoke 0.474354, drought 0.546470 and severity 0.516496, but the source neighbourhood ranks 5/9 at 0.506656. De Kampen ranks first at 0.596843 although its centre is about 5.009 km from the source. The allocator never intersects the source or eligible fuel geometry. This is a reproducibility diagnostic, not an observed fire or current forecast.
findings.action: Label local flame distributions synthetic/unsupported and prohibit rank-based operational use. Prefer an authorised NIPV Risiko-index Natuurbranden export where available; no public documented bulk API, licence or fixed cadence was found. Public fallback can combine BRT TOP10NL eligible land cover (national 1:10,000, CC BY 4.0, editioned releases), a named source/perimeter and timestamp-valid KNMI wind/weather. Tests must prioritize source-intersecting eligible cells and separately expose flame, transported smoke, drought, access, extinguishing-water and suppression assumptions.

findings.summary: A zero coastal-inundation headline can be misread as zero event impact while wind-driven lifeline effects remain active.
findings.evidence: At coastal T+24 GM0376 has floodDepthM=0, current/peak headline severity=0 and spatialEvidence=derived-screening, yet 18.737905 m/s wind produces system pressure 0.241856, 1,858 modeled people under pressure and 10,536 cumulative event-attributable person-hours. By T+72 cumulative burden reaches 38,267. Inspector.tsx:75-76 formats this preset as 0% inundation stress while population and service views remain non-zero. The direct-zero screen is appropriate for open-coast water at this inland municipality, but the combined event interpretation needs explicit component labels.
findings.action: Keep direct seawater stress zero, but present 'no direct coastal inundation in this screen' separately from synthetic wind/indirect lifeline impacts. Exports and rankings must not call the overall event impact-free or attribute affected people to floodwater. Add a cross-view test for zero direct water plus non-zero wind/service consequences and expose component-specific evidence/confidence.

findings.summary: Official water-system context is unusually rich but currently cannot drive Blaricum's drainage availability or recovery.
findings.evidence: E04–E07 document the Laagwaterslootpark nuisance area, a 95%-treated-effluent-fed Gooiergracht, heavy-rain and drought constraints, sewer interaction, target levels, controllable weirs, channel/culvert measures, extra drought pumps and 22 public assets. The model reports compound T+24 drainage availability 0.494095 and river T+24/T+72 availability 0.670375 from generic equations. The official public objects are correctly affectsSimulation=false because no source supplies catchment connectivity, capacities, current controls, receiving-water levels, sewer surcharge, backup or failure/repair state.
findings.action: Retain IMWA/DAMO/GWSW points/areas as partial non-causal context. Request an AGV/municipality licensed hydraulic/stress-test export and approved control relationships for exercises; capture asset ID, catchment, direction, capacity units, scenario level/rain, timestamp, completeness and licence. Where unavailable, build a named editable Gooiergracht exercise subsystem with bounded pump/storage/sewer/backup assumptions and explicit Unknown operational state.

findings.summary: Six roads are transparently labeled logical proxies but cannot represent Blaricum's eight physical lifelines or emergency access.
findings.evidence: The graph contains A27/A1/N527/N526 links with total nominal capacity 1,340. The identical six route IDs appear for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply and each emits transferSemantics logical-proxy. E03 says vital infrastructure is cross-boundary; E05–E07 show actual water transfers follow a different wastewater/Gooiergracht/pump/Eemmeer chain. Static GTFS supplies 13 stop-area records and no ProRail station, but not service operation, evacuation or response capacity.
findings.action: Retain logical-proxy language and never promote NWB capacity to road throughput or physical utility capacity. NWB OGC is Rijkswaterstaat/PDOK road topology, monthly and CC0; timestamp-valid NDW DATEX II can affect only matching mobility/supply segments. Provider WMS and Liander/PWN/Ziggo public data may establish responsibility/context, not state. Use service-specific graphs only from authorised data; otherwise keep capacities editable, sensitivity-tested and synthetic.

findings.summary: Public facility points improve context but do not establish first-72-hour care, shelter, school or supply capacity.
findings.evidence: The public snapshot intersects five DUO education-location records and two KVK public-administration records with GM0376, while no RIVM 2026 acute-care questionnaire point lies inside the boundary. Compound T+24 facilities availability 0.764579 and supply 0.711922 are therefore generic balances. A zero local acute-care point cannot mean zero healthcare need or capacity, and registered schools/offices do not prove emergency role, opening, occupancy, accessibility, staff, generators, food/water stock or patient acceptance.
findings.action: Keep facility layers context-only until authorised continuity data exist. DUO RIO is daily, Creative Commons Attribution (publisher version unspecified); KVK/PDOK government services is Public Domain Mark 1.0 but partial; RIVM acute-care 2026 v1.1 is CC0 and publication/questionnaire-based. Preserve snapshot/role semantics. Seek municipal/GHOR exercise rosters for bounded roles/capacities, never infer shelters or beds from building points.

findings.summary: The sustained-flood guard works, but first-72-hour damage and restoration values have no Blaricum operational calibration.
findings.evidence: River normalized water stress remains 0.457414 through T+72 and compound remains 0.532322; recovery is correctly zero for all eight services while that modeled water persists. River burden rises from 35,120/T+24 to 145,993/T+72 and compound from 121,693 to 476,787. This verifies the no-instant-repair invariant but not the hydraulic screen or magnitudes. E03–E07 provide no event-specific asset damage, backup endurance, staff, stock, access, dispatch, mutual aid, crews, spares or restoration commitment.
findings.action: Keep recovery and intervention controls explicitly scenario-based, time-gated and bounded. Require a selected hydraulic recession plus approved exercise asset/resource fixtures before presenting operational restoration estimates. Missing state stays Unknown; person-hours stay labeled an event-attributable essential-service-pressure proxy rather than customer outage-hours or harm.

findings.summary: Identity, demography, neighbourhood, settlement, public-asset provenance and null semantics are inspectable.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 match GM0376/Blaricum, 12,947 residents, density 1,169, 3,117 residents aged 65-plus and 1,705 one-person households. All nine neighbourhoods, one BAG place and two BRT settlements resolve; the two-person neighbourhood rounding difference and one BAG/generalized-boundary label mismatch are disclosed. Missing district heat/public charging and sparse zero-resident-neighbourhood fields remain null. E07 objects retain source/type/status/timestamp fields and affectsSimulation=false.
findings.action: Retain editions, retrieval timestamps, licences, coverage and null semantics; refresh at source cadence and rerun the focused and national gates after each snapshot.

findings.summary: The full deterministic, causal, exact-zero and layer-invariance contract passes for Blaricum.
findings.evidence: The mandatory harness passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services; zero-intensity output is exact zero; local compound T+24 population/affected/service balances reconcile; causal ledgers close; all eleven layer selections preserve simulation state; event-attributable person-hours are baseline-adjusted and monotonic; and every route says logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain these assertions as regression gates while adding authoritative spatial adapters; do not weaken deterministic, reconciliation or exact-zero behavior to hide calibration gaps.

corrections.summary: Stop exposing Blaricum's generic major-river scalar as supported local inundation and require a selected hydraulic pathway.
corrections.validation: Interim: add an audited GM0376 river note, set direct river spatialEvidence to unsupported and expose local direct water/affected/service consequence as Unknown or numerically neutral for operational use; retain separately labeled Eemmeer/regional-water and indirect network risk. Durable source: LIWO catalogue/API https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 and GeoServer https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows provide expert/professional named depth, arrival and duration scenario layers. LIWO is release/layer-versioned rather than fixed-cadence and the portal states no blanket redistribution licence, so pin scenario/layer/version/retrieval and clear terms before caching. residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, evacuation model, casualty model or operator outage forecast.

No approved GM0376 LIWO/AGV major-river, Eemmeer or regional-defence scenario with connected depth, arrival, duration and recession is ingested; internal floodDepthM is a normalized screening amplitude, not measured local metres.
No licensed native Blaricum/AGV pluvial raster or hydraulic model is ingested for Laagwaterslootpark, Gooiergracht, Bijvanck, Blaricummermeent, sewer surcharge or receiving-water controls.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic hashes do not resolve buildings, terrain depressions, ridge slopes, catchments, forest fuels, households, visitors or individual vulnerability.
Zero CBS resident population in Blaricummer Heide, Eemmeer-Blaricum, Stichtsebrug and Warandepark-De Eng does not imply empty areas during an event; no hourly visitor/occupancy data were invented.
The one BAG Blaricum label outside the CBS generalized polygon is an independently versioned/generalized geometry caveat, not proof of a wrong real administrative boundary.
The public HWH layer is intentionally partial; 22 intersecting points cannot be interpreted as a complete hydraulic/sewer system or current operational state.
Provider polygons identify responsibility at a reference point, not full topology, capacity or state; no drainage provider polygon was returned and fixed-media areas do not represent mobile coverage.
No physical Liander, PWN, drainage, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, live state, backup, priority customers, crews, fuel, spares or restoration estimates are available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
Static NWB and GTFS inputs do not establish live closure, timetable/vehicle operation, congestion, bridge/control state, evacuation throughput or repair access; no ProRail station lies inside GM0376.
Facilities and supply lack verified care roles, beds, staff, patient acceptance, shelters, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Wildfire lacks a selected incident perimeter, current fuel/moisture surface, wind-aware spread, suppression state and resource access; the focused Blaricummer-Heide case is explicitly synthetic.
The Brandweer phase observed on 2 September 2026 is current context only and cannot be applied retrospectively to canonical exercise hours.
Earthquake lacks a selected event, ground-motion surface, local soil/site response and asset fragility; the canonical Groningen source is a synthetic propagation test.
Cyber disruption is a configured exercise without operator incident telemetry, targeted-system inventory or local restoration evidence.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Blaricum resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudburst, surge, fire-spread, dispatch and restriction changes; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
The ten canonical presets omit hazardous-material, pipeline, aviation, water-rescue, infectious-disease and other risks present in the strategic regional risk picture.
